entries.topic: Thiel/Yarvin logic tested; comparative satisfaction with democracy; voter knowledge

claims.text: Pew, 9 Feb-6 May 2026, 16 high-income countries (n=19,715): US 69% dissatisfied with how democracy is working, 30% satisfied; 16-country median 54% dissatisfied; Sweden 24% dissatisfied, Germany 40, Canada 43, Netherlands 44, Australia 48, UK 51, Japan 56, Italy 62, Israel 63, Spain 68, France 69, Greece 77; US Democrats 86% dissatisfied, Republicans 51%; South Korea satisfaction rose 28% to 61% after Yoon's impeachment and an early election

Annenberg (SSRS, Aug 2025, n=1,684): 70% named all three branches of government (65% in 2024, 32% in 2018; 2023 switch from phone to online makes older figures not directly comparable); 13% named none; 21% wrongly said the First Amendment protects the right to bear arms

sources.label: Pew Research Center, 'Americans are more dissatisfied with how their democracy is working than people in other high-income countries', 10 June 2026
Annenberg Public Policy Center, 'Americans' knowledge of civics increases, Annenberg survey finds', September 2025

claims.text: Pew 2026: US satisfaction with democracy 'declined somewhat, from 37% in 2025 to 30% in 2026'; 'This decrease is largely driven by Republicans'; 'Six-in-ten Republicans were satisfied in 2025, compared with 48% today'; Democrats 86% dissatisfied, their satisfaction 'has not changed significantly'
